observations: Photo 0 shows the rear of a black DSLR camera body and a detached lens on bubble wrap.
The camera body has 'Canon' printed on the bottom right of the LCD screen.
The lens barrel is marked 'CANON EF LENS' and '24-105mm 1:4'.
The lens glass appears to have some haze or smudges, and the aperture blades are not visible.
The camera body shows significant wear, scratches, and scuffs on the grip and around the LCD.
The shutter count is not visible in the photo.

claims.evidence: The model name is not legible on the camera body in photo 0.

risks.risk: The camera may not power on or the shutter may be near the end of its life.
risks.proof: A video of the camera powering on and taking a photo.

risks.risk: The lens glass may be scratched or have fungus.
risks.proof: Clear, close-up photos of the front and rear lens elements.

risks.risk: The lens may be a third-party clone rather than a genuine Canon EF lens.
risks.proof: A photo of the lens markings on the barrel.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the camera powering on and taking a photo.
Clear photos of the front and rear lens glass.
Photo of the lens markings on the barrel to confirm authenticity.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
